headline: Dow sinks 1,100 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq tank 2% as Anthropic IPO grabs spotlight
summary: US equities fell sharply on November 19 with the Dow losing ~1,100 points, the S&P 500 dropping 2.02% to 7175.83, and the Nasdaq declining 2.25%. It was the S&P 500's sixth consecutive losing session — its longest losing streak since 2024. Market breadth was extremely negative with 1,222 stocks hitting 52-week lows against only 55 new highs. headline: S&P 500 falls 2% as AI stocks reverse and VIX tops 29 — highest level since March

headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, valuing it at about $1.5tn — the largest IPO in history
summary: Anthropic priced its record-breaking initial public offering at $83 per share, valuing the AI company at approximately $1.5 trillion. The company sold 980 million shares, raising approximately $81 billion — surpassing all prior IPO fundraises in history. Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI assistant, began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19, 2026.

headline: Anthropic IPO: Stock closes first day at $97.17, up 17% from $83 IPO price after 34% opening pop
summary: Anthropic (ANT) opened its first day of trading at $111.50, a 34.3% premium to its $83 IPO price, then faded to close at $97.17 (+17.07%). The stock hit a session high of $115.10 before retreating to a low of $92.72. After the close, shares slipped further to approximately $92.60 in after-hours trading as broader AI sector concerns weighed on market sentiment.

headline: Nasdaq futures fall after Anthropic fails to lift market; ANT pointed ~6% lower in Friday pre-market

CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO while newly appointed board chair Harvey C. Jones leads a search for a permanent successor.

Non-GAAP EPS of $2.68 beat the $2.47 consensus estimate. Data Center revenue reached $107.6 billion. These were the first results reported under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's resignation on November 12.

headline: Fed came close to an October rate hike; FOMC minutes show two members favored 25bps increase
summary: The Federal Reserve held its target rate at 3.75%-4.00% at the October 27-28 FOMC meeting, though two dissenting members favored a 25 basis point increase. The November 18 release of FOMC minutes described the hold decision as a 'close call,' with nearly all participants agreeing that future rate increases will be needed to achieve the 2% inflation objective.

Some members viewed a hike as appropriate in October while nearly all agreed the committee would need to raise rates in the future. Market reaction pushed December hike odds to near 100%.

headline: Markets now price 100% odds of Fed rate hike in December; some see risk of a 50bps move
summary: Interest rate futures markets priced in a 100% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting, up from 67% one week prior, following hot economic data and hawkish Fed commentary. The base case is 25 basis points, but some market participants see a roughly 10% chance of a larger 50 basis point move if inflation data remain hot.

headline: US October PPI +0.3% MoM; 12-month rate climbs to 6.5% — highest since November 2022
summary: US producer prices rose 0.3% month-over-month in October, slightly below the 0.4% forecast, but the 12-month rate climbed to 6.5%, the highest since November 2022. Core PPI (excluding food, energy, and trade services) rose 0.5% month-over-month for a second consecutive month and was up 4.9% year-over-year, with inflation described as broadening out.
